content.text:
## Root cause

`Cache.addAll()` (which `Cache.add()` delegates to) awaits a promise that is only settled from fetch's `processResponseEndOfBody` callback. In `fetchFinale` (`lib/web/fetch/index.js:1143`) undici deliberately skips the spec's identity transform stream and instead waits on `finished(internalResponse.body.stream, …)`. That only fires once the body stream ends — and nothing in `addAll` ever read the body, so for any response with a body the fetch never reached its end-of-body steps and `add`/`addAll` hung forever.

A second, latent problem: even if the promise had settled, the response stored in the cache would have been the live, undrained network stream, so a later `match()` body read would be unreliable.

## Fix — `lib/web/cache/cache.js`

- In `addAll`'s `processResponse`, once the response passes the status and `vary` checks, clone it (`cloneResponse`, teeing the body) and read the original body to completion via a new `readResponseBody` helper. This is exactly what `Cache.put` already does: draining the stream lets fetch finish, and the teed clone keeps the bytes so the cached response replays. `processResponseEndOfBody` now resolves with that clone, setting `body.source` to the read bytes for parity with `put`.
- Guarded `processResponseEndOfBody` for the case where `processResponse` already rejected (bad status / `vary: *`), so the late end-of-body callback is a no-op rather than dereferencing a null promise.
- Added `cancelResponseBody` on the invalid-status path: previously that body was left undrained, holding the connection open.

## Tests — `test/cache/cache.js`

Added a suite against a local server covering: `add` resolving and caching a re-readable body, `addAll` over several URLs plus a bodyless 204, rejection on non-ok status, rejection on `vary: *`, and a mixed batch caching nothing when one request fails. All pass (`node --test test/cache/cache.js`), as do `test/cache/cachestorage.js` and `test/cache/get-field-values.js`.

Notes on the repo's risk map: the edit is confined to `lib/web/cache/cache.js`, which is not a listed hotspot and is not in any `co_change` or `seams` pair (the `cache-handler.js` ↔ `interceptor/cache.js` coupling is the HTTP cache interceptor, a separate subsystem — unchanged). `lib/web/fetch/index.js` is a hotspot but needed no change; the behaviour it documents (`finished()` instead of the transform stream) is what the cache layer now accommodates. COMPLEX.md says the real coverage for this area is the WPT suite — the `test/web-platform-tests/wpt` submodule is not checked out in this worktree, so I could not run it; the WPT `service-workers/cache-storage` tests should be run in CI before merging. Nothing is committed.
